_note: Shown on Today, one of each per day (picked by date). Kid-facing: two lines max, verbs first. Fuel lines are general habits for young athletes, not a diet; anything medical goes to a doctor or dietitian.
cheers: Small bites. Big dancer.
You don't have to feel ready. Just start.
One clean run beats five rushed ones.
Hannah built it. You own it.
Nerves mean you care. Breathe and go.
Progress hides in boring days. Today counts.
Pointed feet are a choice. Choose them.
Eyes up. The judges can't see your feet if they're looking at your face.
Tired is fine. Quitting is not.
You already know more than you did last week.
Dance it like someone you love is watching.
Mistakes are rehearsal. Keep going.
Strong legs, soft landings.
Five minutes is a win. Take the win.
Be the dancer who finishes the shape.
Yesterday is done. Today is yours.
Breathe out, reach long.
Clean beats fancy. Every time.
Your streak is proof. Keep the proof.
Smile first. The body follows.
mind: Pick ONE thing to fix today. Not five.
Before a run, say the story once in your head.
Breathe out longer than you breathe in. Three times.
Pick a spot above the judges. That's where your eyes live.
If you mess up, finish the shape anyway. Nobody saw it but you.
Say 'I get to', not 'I have to'.
Picture the ending before you start the beginning.
Count out loud when it feels fast.
Nervous and excited feel the same. Call it excited.
Tell yourself one true thing you did well. Every day.
Hard day? Make the practice shorter, not skipped.
Rest is training too. Sleep is when you get stronger.
Compare you to you last month. Nobody else.
When you walk on, you've already done the work.
fuel: Water bottle in your dance bag. Sip before, during, after.
Eat a real breakfast on dance days. Eggs, oats or toast with something on it.
A snack 1–2 hours before class: banana, yogurt, crackers and cheese.
After class, eat within an hour: something with protein and something with carbs.
Fruit or veg with every meal. Colors on the plate.
Sleepy at practice? Check: did you drink water today?
Comp day: pack snacks you've eaten before. No new foods.
Milk, yogurt or cheese every day: dancers' bones need it.
Dinner after a late class, even a small one. Don't go to bed empty.
Sports drinks are for long hot days. Water is for everything else.
Eat enough. Growing dancers need more food, not less.
A treat is fine. It's fuel too, just not the only fuel.
Long rehearsal? Bring two snacks, not one.
Bedtime on a school night: nine to ten hours. That's the secret trick.
